standard_prerequisites: Context span 1042-1083: Badam-Baplan construction - a valuation ring R is coherent (Algebra, example-valuation-ring-coherent) so R[[x]] is flat over R (Algebra, proposition-characterize-coherent); and the same-section lemma proving: if R[[x]] is flat over R[x] for a domain R with fraction field K, then R is normal iff completely normal (almost-integral elements detected via (ax-b)f = -rb and the faithfully flat localization at S = {h : h(0)=1})
Valuation rings are normal (Algebra, lemma-valuation-ring-normal); almost integral elements: ralpha^n in R for all n
core_obligations: By the context lemma it suffices to show R is not completely normal (valuation rings are normal by the Algebra lemma)
Pick a prime chain p properly contained in m in R, a nonzero x in p and y in m \setminus p
xy^{-n} in R for all n >= 1 (else y^n/x in R, absurd since y not in p); hence 1/y is almost integral over R but not in R, so R is not completely normal and R[[x]] is not flat over R[x]
proof_roadmap: Reduce non-flatness over R[x] to failure of complete normality via the context lemma
Choose the two-prime chain and witnesses x, y
Prove 1/y is almost integral over R but outside R, concluding non-flatness
